name: mf-agent
description: A lightweight, clean-room coding agent for VS Code: graph memory, strong editing tools, native POSIX commands, browser testing and MCP — with a compiled Go core.

mfagent.memory.enabled.description: Enable the persistent graph memory for this workspace. The database lives at .mfagent/memory.db.

mfagent.shell.useTerminal.markdownDescription: Run the agent's shell commands in a visible VS Code terminal, using your own configured shell, profile and PATH, instead of a process the agent spawns on its own. Requires terminal shell integration; the agent falls back to spawning a shell when it is unavailable. Background queue workers always spawn their own shell regardless of this setting.

mfagent.mcpServers.markdownDescription: MCP servers to connect. Each entry takes either `command` + `args` (stdio) or `url` (streamable HTTP). Merged with any servers in your VS Code user `mcp.json`, which needs no entry here at all — pick which of either source are active for a project from the Task Queue view's Context tab.

mfagent.queue.mode.description: lockstep = validate before next task. continuous = executors run ahead while conclusion checks follow.

mfagent.queue.cronIntervalSeconds.markdownDescription: How often, in seconds, the supervisor loop wakes to read the `tasks` and `agent_logs` tables: picking up finished work, noticing a worker that has gone quiet, and deciding whether a task continues, stops, is broken down, or goes to verification. A tick that finds nothing new costs a few database reads; a full review of live work is rate-limited separately by `#mfagent.queue.reviewIntervalSeconds#`. A task list that sets its own interval in the Task Queue view overrides this.

mfagent.queue.liveLogKeep.markdownDescription: Live-output rows kept per task in the `agent_logs` table — the streamed text, reasoning and tool calls the Task Queue view shows as each agent works. Older rows are pruned as new ones arrive; the durable journal the supervisor reads (`task_events`) is not affected.

mfagent.queue.workerSilentMinutes.markdownDescription: How long a running worker may write nothing before it is treated as dead and its task requeued. This is not a time limit on the task: a live worker writes an activity record every `#mfagent.activityIntervalSeconds#` even while it waits on the model, so only a process that has actually stopped goes quiet for this long. Raise it if you see healthy workers being requeued.

mfagent.activityIntervalSeconds.description: How often a working agent records what it is doing. These records are the queue's evidence that work is progressing, and they are kept per task.

mfagent.llm.idleMinutes.description: How long a model reply may deliver nothing at all before the connection is treated as dropped. This is not a limit on how long a reply may take — every byte received resets it, so a slow local model can stream for hours.

mfagent.llm.maxContextTokens.markdownDescription: Context tokens (input plus cache) one round may carry before the core stops the tool loop and asks the agent for a handoff report. This is not a budget for the work: it is the backstop for a queue turn that runs with no round ceiling, and it exists so an agent that keeps calling tools without converging stops just short of the provider refusing the request — handing its supervisor an account of what it did instead of an API error. Raise it for a large-context model; set it to `-1` to switch it off.

mfagent.queue.reviewIntervalSeconds.markdownDescription: How often the supervisor may look in on a task that is still executing. Each look is a full model turn over the task's journal, so on a task that legitimately runs for hours a review on every `#mfagent.queue.cronIntervalSeconds#` tick is mostly re-reading evidence it has already judged. A review is skipped entirely when the journal has not grown since the last one, and this interval is never applied to a task that has stopped and is waiting on a decision.

mfagent.queue.workerMaxRounds.description: Tool rounds per executor or verifier turn. At the limit, preserve progress and hand off to automatic supervisor recovery; this never counts as a passing check.

mfagent.queue.maxContextTokens.description: Context ceiling for queue workers, additionally capped by llm.maxContextTokens. A conservative default for local models; set at or below your inference server context size.

mfagent.queue.maxRounds.markdownDescription: Tool-calling round budget for planning agents. Task execution and formal validation use queue.workerMaxRounds; repeated identical tool failures still stop after three occurrences.

mfagent.queue.maxFilesPerRegion.markdownDescription: Largest file count one region of the workspace may hold before the deterministic scan splits it further. This is what bounds how much a phase's expansion agent has to explore in one sitting, regardless of how large the whole project is — see the Plan tab. Lower it if expansions on a dense codebase keep getting cut off; raise it to produce fewer, coarser phases on a small one.

mfagent.queue.supervisorMaxRounds.description: Compatibility ceiling for supervisor replies. Supervisors receive no tools and normally finish in one conclusion-only response.

mfagent.queue.notifyCommand.markdownDescription: Command run when an autonomous run finishes, with a JSON summary (`event`, `verified`, `total`, `usage`, `workspaceRoot`, `at`) as its one argument — e.g. a script that sends a desktop or Slack notification. Left empty (the default), nothing runs; the queue still shows an in-editor notification either way, which is only useful if someone is watching the editor when it lands.

mfagent.queue.claudeCli.maxBudgetUsd.markdownDescription: Dollar cap passed as `--max-budget-usd` to each Planner/Supervisor turn run through the Claude CLI provider — it has no round-count ceiling of its own the way mfcore turns do (`#mfagent.queue.maxRounds#`). Set to 0 to remove the cap.

scripts.build: npm run build:core && npm run build:ext
